app.title: Hyperscale Landscapes
app.tagline: Open Tools for Visualising AI Data Infrastructures in Place
step.export: Download or export for digital media, websites, 2D or 3D print
pick.sites.help: Based on the open map data maintained by the Association for the Protection of Rural Scotland (APRS).
geology.note.head: What is data and what is drawn
geology.note.data: Data (BGS): where each rock unit, superficial deposit and coal resource meets the walls; borehole positions and depths; pit positions and names; seam names on mine plans.
geology.note.assumed: Assumed: rock contacts carried straight down; sheets and superficial deposits drawn at nominal thickness ({thicknesses}).
geology.note.schematic: Schematic: the number, spacing and thickness of coal seams; rock patterns.
geology.note.boreholes: {n} BGS boreholes within 50 m of a wall
geology.note.boreholes.deepest: {n} BGS boreholes within 50 m of a wall, deepest {ref} ({depth} m)
geology.note.pits: Pit squares are 50 m symbols, not footprints or hazard zones.
pick.sites.aprs: APRS map of proposed data centres in Scotland
pick.search.privacy: Searching sends your words to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service.
pick.upload.help: GeoJSON, KML or KMZ. The file stays on your device.
pick.toolarge: This area is {w} × {h} km. The browser can build up to about 3 × 3 km (9 km²). For larger areas, use the Python tool.
pick.large: Above about 3 km across, buildings become hard to make out at 150–200 mm.
size.exag.note: Hills are drawn {x} times taller than they are, so they show at this scale. Every download says so.
context.layer.why: The land up to {km} km beyond the model: Copernicus 30 m terrain, with the main roads, railways, water, buildings and place names from OpenStreetMap, faded with distance. Shown on screen only; it is never part of the print, and nothing inside the model area comes from it. While it is on, the camera stays above the terrain and the soil sides and geology walls are switched off.
energy.layer.why: The electricity network up to {km} km beyond the model: pylons, poles and overhead lines from OpenStreetMap, at recorded heights where known. Shown on screen only, never printed. While it is on, the camera stays above the terrain and the soil sides and geology walls are switched off.
layer.scale.why: The length of ground the bar covers across the screen at the centre of the view. It changes as you zoom and is left out of saved images.
pits.coal.why: Solid dark squares. A BritPits record counts as a coal mine when its name matches a BGS coal mine plan, the record gives coal, or the name is a colliery (labelled “colliery · no mine plan matched”). Closed mines and quarries recorded by the British Geological Survey (BritPits). Each square is a 50 m symbol at the recorded point, not a footprint or hazard zone. Screen only.
pits.unknown.why: Dashed squares: BritPits records whose type the record does not give, and whose name matches no coal mine plan. Closed mines and quarries recorded by the British Geological Survey (BritPits). Each square is a 50 m symbol at the recorded point, not a footprint or hazard zone. Screen only.
pits.quarry.why: Outlined squares: BritPits records of quarries, including pits whose name only matched a coal mine plan once “Quarry” was taken off it (labelled “name also on a coal mine plan”). Off by default. Closed mines and quarries recorded by the British Geological Survey (BritPits). Each square is a 50 m symbol at the recorded point, not a footprint or hazard zone. Screen only.
props.trees.why: One symbol per detected crown (thinned to the tallest per 10 m cell), with height and crown width from a canopy height model: Scottish Public Sector LiDAR, gaps filled from the Meta/WRI global canopy height map. Tree type from OpenStreetMap, the Native Woodland Survey of Scotland or the National Forest Inventory, in that order, else broadleaf. Drawn taller by the slider factor. Screen only: trees are not in the print files.
layer.electricity.why: Substations, generators, battery storage, overhead lines, pylons, poles and wind turbines, shown and hidden together. Overhead lines are drawn between their supports where the supports are known; they are not painted along the ground. The print keeps its raised power-line strip.
props.turbines.why: Turbine positions from OpenStreetMap, drawn at true height. Hub height and rotor size are from the OpenStreetMap record where given, otherwise a curated or typical value (the caption counts these). Rotors face the OpenStreetMap direction, otherwise the prevailing south-westerly wind. Screen only.
props.pylons.why: Pylons, poles and overhead lines from OpenStreetMap, drawn at true height. Heights are from the record where given, otherwise a typical height for the structure and voltage. The sag between supports is drawn, not measured. Screen only.
export.3mf.help: Opens in Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer and PrusaSlicer with colours assigned.
export.lowres: Browser downloads are lower resolution than the Python tool's. For planning hearings or exhibitions, ask someone to run the Python tool.
caption.exag: Height exaggerated ×{x}; buildings at true height
